searchText: Big PR with lot's of basic tests for most defined `eth` methods (skipped some methods related to mining and signing), fixed several small spec issues, added `eth_createAccessList -- PTAL https://github.com/ethereum/execution-apis/pull/265 will leave up for at least 24 hrs It would be good to know if these have been run against multiple clients or not. I'm a bit hesitant about specifying things by "what geth does", especially when what geth doese isn't reasonable (not common, but sometimes this is the case). By running the suite against other clients, we can find out where they differ and then initially PR everything where there is consensus, and discuss items where there isn't. (glancing over these tests, nothing jumps out as "probably going to cause cross client problems") these tests power the hive test `rpc-compat` so once it is merged will see how other clients fair: https://hivetests2.ethdevops.io/ im having some trouble running hive locally right now, but i expect there to be many failures as the tests verification is pretty rigid (e.g. no extra fields beyond what is specified) I'm not proposing this is the final form of the spec for these methods, but rather we use this as a tool to continue honing the spec (this is why it is still in alpha) Ah, OK. If this is just step one towards reconciliation then I support it. I thought this was proposing to be The Standard. that comes later, when we move out of alpha
